title: SSH Fleet Doctor
summary: An evolving SSH administration and server-health toolkit combining Bash automation with a Python/Paramiko monitor for authorized remote systems.

sections.label: Overview
sections.title: Operational visibility through a small, inspectable toolkit.
paragraphs: The project began as SSH-Infiltrator and is evolving into SSH Fleet Doctor. It joins a Bash-based control workflow with a Python command-line monitor for remote resource checks and administrative tasks.
Its public documentation describes health monitoring, logging, backups, reporting, multi-server work, and error handling.

sections.label: Capabilities
sections.title: Connect, inspect, record, and respond.
points: Inspect CPU, memory, disk, and network statistics
Execute selected or custom administrative commands
Record actions for auditing and troubleshooting
Support scheduled tasks, file backup, and system reports

sections.label: Architecture
sections.title: Shell orchestration with a Paramiko-based Python path.
paragraphs: SETUP.sh creates a Python environment and installs Paramiko. SSH_Infiltrator.sh provides the interactive shell workflow, while python/SSH_Intruder.py accepts host and username arguments and prompts for a password when one is not supplied.

sections.label: Safety
sections.title: Administrative power requires explicit boundaries.
paragraphs: The tool can invoke disruptive remote operations. It should only be used on systems you own or are explicitly authorized to administer, beginning with a disposable test host. SSH keys and a restricted account are preferable to passing passwords on the command line.
sections.callout: Never point the toolkit at an unknown or production host until every enabled action has been reviewed.

architecture.title: SSH Fleet Doctor component map
architecture.summary: The repository combines an interactive Bash administration layer, a Python/Paramiko monitoring client, environment setup, logging, and release automation.
steps: SETUP.sh checks for Python and pip, creates a virtual environment, activates it, and installs Paramiko.
SSH_Infiltrator.sh provides the historical interactive control workflow for connections, commands, monitoring, backups, scheduling, and reports.
python/SSH_Intruder.py validates the supplied IP address, creates an SSH client, prompts for credentials when needed, and exposes resource-monitoring and custom-command functions.
Local log files record tool actions for troubleshooting and audit review; sensitive credentials should never be committed to those files.
The tool boundary is an explicitly authorized SSH host. A restricted remote user and SSH keys should be used for any environment beyond a disposable lab.

validation.title: SSH Fleet Doctor preflight checks
validation.summary: Static and disposable-host checks for the public Bash and Python clients before any authorized operational trial.
checks: Run bash -n against SETUP.sh and SSH_Infiltrator.sh, and compile-check python/SSH_Intruder.py without connecting to a host.
Create the virtual environment and confirm Paramiko imports successfully from the activated environment.
Reject malformed IP input and confirm omitted passwords are requested interactively rather than written to shell history.
Use a disposable SSH host to verify read-only CPU, memory, disk, and network monitoring before testing administrative actions.
Confirm logs contain useful operational context without credentials or other secrets.
Exercise timeout, refused connection, invalid credential, and lost-session paths; verify the client exits safely and explains the failure.
